t: Living a Blessed Life
v: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, and humble.
Don’t repay evil for evil, or insult for insult; but instead, bless, because you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.
For, “He who would love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
Let him turn away from evil and do good. Let him seek peace, and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears open to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
b: In this teaching, Peter shows that believers are meant to live with a character that sets them apart. By saying “Finally,” he gives a closing call: in the way we treat one another, we are to be of one mind, sympathetic, loving, and marked by compassion and humility.

When others wrong us or hurl insults, our response should not be revenge but a choice to bless. We were called for this very purpose. It is not to win arguments or defend ourselves, but to become channels of blessing and to inherit the blessing that comes from God.

The passage also tells us to guard our tongues, speaking no evil and no deceit. The truly good life belongs to the person who chooses to turn from evil and do good, to seek peace, and to keep his focus on the Lord. For the Lord watches over the righteous and hears their prayers, but his face is turned against those who do evil.
a: Bless instead of retaliating
In the midst of hurt and conflict, learn not to repay evil with evil, but to choose to bless the other person.
Speak gracious words, not harsh ones
Keeping a watch over your tongue is a practical expression of a godly life.
Live out the power of peace
The Lord delights to hear the prayers of the righteous. As we pursue peace, we will also experience God’s presence and blessing.
q: When others hurt me, do I tend to strike back with harsh words, or am I willing to choose blessing?
Are my words and attitudes becoming a channel for God’s blessing to others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, You have called me to live a different kind of life, not one of angry arguments, but one that chooses blessing by Your grace. Please help me to control my tongue, to refuse evil words, and to live in peace and kindness. May my life be pleasing in Your sight and become a blessing to others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Embrace of Coming Home
v: But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.
I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
“He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight. I am no more worthy to be called your son.’
“But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat, and celebrate;
for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ They began to celebrate.
b: In his deep hunger and despair, the prodigal son finally came to his senses. He remembered that even his father’s hired servants had food to eat, while he was wandering far from home and nearly starving. He decided to get up and go back. He no longer dared hope to be a son; he only hoped to be received as a servant.

But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him, ran to him, and held him tightly. Before the son could finish his confession, the father told his servants to bring a robe, a ring, and sandals, restoring him to his place as a son. He even killed the fattened calf and celebrated with everyone, because this lost son had come home.

This parable is Jesus’ deepest portrait of the Father’s heart. God is not waiting to judge our failures. He is eagerly waiting for us to turn back, running to meet us and embrace us, glad to forgive and restore.
a: God gladly receives the repentant
No matter how far we have wandered, if we turn back, he always welcomes us with open arms.
Lay down shame and bravely come home
We do not need to earn God’s love by our performance. We need only humbly confess, and he will show us grace.
Forgiveness is the Father’s nature
This also reminds us to treat those who repent with the same kindness our Father shows to us.
q: Am I still drifting far away, afraid to come back to my Father?
Do I truly believe that God accepts me, and am I willing to forgive others as well?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for always waiting for me and loving me, even when I have wandered from You. Please forgive my past rebellion and weakness, and help me to come back to You with courage. May I also learn to see others through Your eyes, and to give them kindness and acceptance. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: From Bitter Water to Sweet Spring
v: Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur. They went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
When they came to Marah, they couldn’t drink from the waters of Marah, for they were bitter. Therefore its name was called Marah.
The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”
He cried to the Lord. The Lord showed him a tree. When he threw it into the waters, the waters were made sweet. There he made a statute and an ordinance for them, and there he tested them;

and he said, “If you will diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have put on the Egyptians; for I am the Lord who heals you.”
They came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They encamped there by the waters.
b: Israel had just experienced the miracle of the Red Sea, yet three days into the wilderness they could find no water. They came to Marah and found the water too bitter to drink, and they quickly complained to Moses. Moses turned to God, and God showed him a tree. When he threw it into the water, the bitter water became sweet. This was not only a miracle of provision, but also a test of faith.

Through this, God taught his people that if they would listen to him and keep his statutes, they would experience healing and protection. God revealed himself as “the Lord who heals you,” which speaks not only of physical healing but of the renewing and restoring of faith deep within.

After the bitter waters of Marah, they came to Elim, with its twelve springs and seventy palm trees, a picture of rest and abundance. God does not simply leave us in suffering; he leads us through trials into renewal and provision.
a: Turn to God in hard times
Instead of complaining about circumstances, learn to cry out to God as Moses did.
Trust God’s healing and guidance
The bitter water made sweet reminds us that God can turn our situation around even when it seems hopeless.
Prepare your heart to obey God’s word
The promises of blessing and healing are prepared for those who wholeheartedly follow the Lord.
q: Have I complained in hardship instead of first coming to God for help?
Do I believe God can turn the bitter waters in my life into sweetness?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for never leaving me in the wilderness. Even though I am often weak and complaining, You still lead me with grace. Please help me to look to You in hard times and to believe that You can turn bitterness into sweetness and bring healing to the sick. May I wholeheartedly obey Your word and experience Your faithful provision and healing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Praising the King of Love and Glory
v: (A praise psalm by David.) I will exalt you, my God, the King. I will praise your name forever and ever.
Every day I will praise you. I will extol your name forever and ever.
Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable.
One generation will commend your works to another, and will declare your mighty acts.
I will meditate on the glorious majesty of your honor, and on your wondrous works.
Men will speak of the might of your awesome acts. I will declare your greatness.
They will utter the memory of your great goodness, and will sing of your righteousness.
The Lord is gracious, and merciful; slow to anger, and of great loving kindness.
b: This is a psalm of praise by David, and it opens with a heart of worship: “I will exalt you, my God, the King.” The psalmist gives his whole life, day after day without ceasing, to praising God’s name, and calls on every generation to proclaim his greatness.

He marvels that God’s works are beyond measure, and that each generation should tell the next of his wonders and power. He meditates on the glory of God’s majesty and recalls his grace, righteousness, and goodness. This kind of worship is more than a personal expression of feeling; it is a living testimony passed down from one generation to the next.

The psalmist goes on to reveal God’s nature: he is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in loving kindness. This almighty King is not only great and glorious but also full of gentleness and love, worthy of our praise for a lifetime.
a: Make praise a daily habit
Learn to praise God not only in meetings, but in every day of your life.
Pass faith down through the generations
Tell the next generation of God’s works and grace, and be a blessing to your family and community.
Meditate on God’s character
He is not only great but full of mercy and love, worth knowing and imitating with all our hearts.
q: Do I praise God every day, or only thank him when I feel moved to?
In my family or church, do I take the initiative to tell of God’s grace so the next generation will know him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I will praise You every day, for Your name deserves great praise. Your works are wonderful, and Your love never ends. Teach me to praise You not only in good times but also in hard times, meditating on Your faithfulness, and to pass on Your glory to the next generation. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Spiritual Inheritance and the God Who Is With Us
v: Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went, and stood opposite them at a distance; and they two stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took his mantle, and wrapped it together, and struck the waters, and they were divided here and there, so that they two went over on dry ground.
When they had gone over, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you, before I am taken from you.” Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me.”
He said, “You have asked a hard thing. Nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so.”
As they still went on, and talked, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, which separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
Elisha saw it, and he cried, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” He saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes, and tore them in two pieces.
He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of the Jordan.

He took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and struck the waters, and said, “Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah?” When he also had struck the waters, they were divided here and there; and Elisha went over.
b: As Elijah was about to be taken up to heaven, Elisha stayed close to him, showing his hunger for God and for the prophetic calling. The two walked together by the Jordan and witnessed God’s wonderful work: Elijah struck the water with his mantle and it divided, a sign of spiritual authority at work.

In their last moments together, Elisha asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit. This was not greed, but a sincere longing for spiritual power. Elijah told him that if he saw him taken up, he would receive what he asked.

God was faithful. As a chariot and horses of fire separated the two and Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind, Elisha saw it with his own eyes and tore his clothes in grief and change. When he picked up Elijah’s mantle and struck the Jordan again, the water divided once more, proving that he had received God’s Spirit and mission.
This passage bears witness to the passing on of spiritual authority. It also shows us that God is not only with great prophets; he is glad to fill with his Spirit all who long to follow him.
a: Long for spiritual gifts
Like Elisha, ask not for position but for more of the anointing and power that come from God.
Follow closely in God’s presence
Even when you cannot see the road ahead, be willing to walk faithfully where the Lord leads.
Take up the mission, not in your own strength
Remember that God’s presence and calling bring all the power needed to complete the task he entrusts to us.
q: Do I sincerely long for the power and anointing that come from God?
When I face a spiritual handing-over or a new season, do I believe God will be with me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I long to follow You wholeheartedly as Elisha did, and to receive the spiritual gifts and power that come from You. When You call me to take up a mission, let Your Spirit move me deeply, so that I may be strong and courageous, acting not in my own strength but in Your presence and power. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The God Who Carries Us to the End
v: “Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been borne by me from their birth, who have been carried from the womb;
and even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs will I carry you. I have made, and I will bear; yes, I will carry, and will deliver.
“To whom will you liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, that we may be like?
Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver in the balance. They hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god. They fall down, yes, they worship.
They bear it on the shoulder. They carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands. From its place it will not move. Yes, one may cry to it, yet it can’t answer, nor save him out of his trouble.
“Remember this, and show yourselves men! Bring it again to mind, you transgressors.
Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me;”
b: Through the prophet Isaiah, God calls to Israel with a gentle but firm voice: “You have been borne by me from your birth, carried from the womb.” This is an eternal God who has held his people from the beginning of life until old age and gray hair.

In contrast are the idols made by human hands. Though they are fashioned from gold and silver and worshiped, they are powerless; they cannot answer prayer or save anyone from trouble. God reminds his people that the true God is one of a kind, in control of history since creation, who not only made us but will carry us to the very end.

God invites his people to remember what he has done in the past, his unchanging faithfulness and power, and to turn from false securities and rely on the one true God, who is the same from beginning to end.
a: Rest in God’s arms
No matter how old we are or how many storms we have been through, God never changes. He still says, “I will carry, and will deliver.”
Refuse false securities
People often depend on money, position, or their own ability, forgetting that none of these can truly save us. Only God is a dependable refuge.
Remember God’s faithfulness and works
In difficulty or confusion, look back at how God has guided and carried you, and your faith will be strengthened again.
q: When I feel tired and powerless, do I believe God is still carrying me and will not abandon me?
Is there an “idol” in my life that I depend on but that cannot save me? Am I willing to turn back and look to the one true God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for carrying me since I was in my mother’s womb and for never leaving me, even into old age. Please help me not to rely on empty things, but to fix my eyes on You and remember Your faithfulness and deliverance. May I rest in Your arms all my life and trust You to the end. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Call to Unity and a Life Put into Practice
v: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love;
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body, and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling;
one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all.
b: Writing as a prisoner for the Lord, Paul earnestly urges believers: since you have been called, live a life worthy of that calling. This calling is not abstract; it is concrete. We are to treat one another with humility, gentleness, patience, and love.

True unity is not kept by systems or slogans, but by the heart of unity the Spirit gives, bound together in peace and carefully guarded. Paul then names the foundation of our faith: “one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God.” All of this stresses that the church is already one in the Lord, and we are called to live out that spiritual reality.
a: Live out the worth of your calling
We have not only been saved; we have been called to live a life worthy of Christ, in character and conduct bearing witness to the Lord’s grace.
Keep unity through love
Church unity comes from bearing with one another in love, not from demanding perfection. Learn to start with yourself and become a peacemaker.
Be joined together in truth
We have the same Lord, the same faith, and the same hope. So remind yourself often that we are joined not by outward labels but by the Spirit within.
q: Are my words and actions worthy of the calling I have received?
In my church and relationships, am I working hard to keep the unity the Spirit gives?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for calling me into Your Kingdom. Please help me to live a life worthy of that calling, humble and patient in everything, keeping unity with peace and love. May I live not for myself, but as a vessel of unity and witness, so that others see Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God’s Promise of a New Thing and the Grace of Forgiveness
v: “Don’t remember the former things, nor consider the things of old.
Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
The animals of the field will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I give water in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
the people which I formed for myself, that they may declare my praise.
Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; but you have been weary of me, Israel.
You have not brought me of your sheep for your burnt offerings; neither have you honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
You have bought me no sweet cane with money, nor have you filled me with the fat of your sacrifices; but you have burdened me with your sins. You have wearied me with your iniquities.
I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
b: Through the prophet, the Lord calls to his people: do not keep living in the past, and do not be bound by former mistakes or former glories. He is about to do a new thing, making a way in the midst of hardship and bringing rivers of life out of dry ground. This new thing is not a human plan; it is God’s own work, a path of grace prepared for his people.

Though God treated them so kindly, Israel was cold toward him, did not worship, and even grew weary of him. They no longer brought offerings or honored God from the heart, and instead burdened him with their sins. Yet astonishingly, God still says, “I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.”

This passage shows us deeply that God does not give grace according to our performance. Out of his own love and glory, he takes the initiative to forgive, renew, and save. He longs for us to respond to his love and his works not with empty ritual, but with sincere hearts.
a: Embrace the new thing God is doing
Do not live in past pain, failure, or pride. God is doing a new thing and will open a path of grace in the barren places of your life.
Respond sincerely to God’s grace
Not merely with outward religious acts, but with love and thanksgiving toward the God who takes the initiative to forgive sins.
Believe that God’s forgiveness is real
When you are willing to turn to him, however weak you have been, God is willing to “not remember” your sins and give you a fresh start.
q: Am I still trapped by past failures or hurts, unable to see the new road God wants to open for me?
Am I willing to respond with a sincere heart to God’s love that forgives and renews?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not treating me according to my sins, but for taking the initiative to forgive me and open a new way for me. Please help me not to stay in past failures and debts, but to embrace by faith the new thing You are doing. Let me worship You with thanksgiving and a sincere heart, and live a life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Beautiful Pattern of a Spiritual Community
v: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,
that you receive her in the Lord, in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, and of my own self.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
who for my life, laid down their own necks; to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the assemblies of the Gentiles.
Greet the assembly that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the first fruits of Asia to Christ.
Greet Mary, who labored much for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junias, my relatives, and my fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet them who are of the household of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my relative. Greet them of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
b: At the close of his letter, Paul mentions, one by one, brothers and sisters who served faithfully in the Lord. He does not hurry to finish; he names them individually, expressing respect and thanks. This shows that the church is not only about each person’s relationship with God, but about a community joined together and building one another up.

Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchreae, was trusted and often helped others. Priscilla and Aquila not only worked alongside Paul but risked their lives for him. Mary, Junia, Tryphaena, Tryphosa, and others also labored hard for the Lord. Paul overlooks no one who is faithful in the Lord, for he knows each is a precious member of God’s household.

This passage reminds us that in God’s family, everyone who serves faithfully is remembered by God, and we should honor and thank one another. The church does not depend on a few leaders alone, but on everyone serving the Lord together in unity, bearing witness to his love and truth.
a: Treasure your spiritual companions
Do not think faith is only between you and God. God calls us to live in community, supporting one another and serving together.
Learn to affirm and give thanks
Like Paul, learn to express gratitude, and say a word of “Thank you!” to those members who quietly give and serve faithfully.
Be a blessing to others
Whatever our position, we can be like Phoebe, Priscilla, and Tryphosa, blessing others with love and faithfulness and becoming a strength to the church.
q: Who are the spiritual companions in my life to whom I should express thanks?
Am I willing to become a spiritual partner like these people: faithful, hardworking, and glad to give?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not letting me walk the heavenly road alone, but giving me a spiritual family to support me. Please help me to learn thankfulness and honor, to treasure every member who works with me in the Lord. May I, like Phoebe, Priscilla, and Mary, serve willingly and faithfully to the end, so that Your church is made stronger and Your name is glorified. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Spirit of Truth and the Lord Who Gives Peace
v: “If you love me, keep my commandments.
I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever,
the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive; for it doesn’t see him, neither knows him. You know him, for he lives with you, and will be in you.
“I have said these things to you, while still living with you.
But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, do I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
You heard how I told you, ‘I go away, and I come to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced, because I said ‘I am going to the Father;’ for the Father is greater than I.
Now I have told you before it happens, that when it happens, you may believe.
I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world comes, and he has nothing in me.
But that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let us go from here.”
b: At the supper before his departure, Jesus revealed a deep and deeply comforting truth: he would not leave us as orphans, but promised to send the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, to be with us forever. The Spirit is the Spirit of truth. Though the world cannot receive him, believers know him, because he lives in us and guides us along the Lord’s way.

At the same time, Jesus left a most precious gift: “My peace.” This peace is not the calm of outward circumstances, but a rest that comes from God and carries us through storms. He encouraged his disciples not to be troubled or afraid, because everything he did came from love for the Father and complete obedience to him.
His words, the presence of the Holy Spirit, and the peace he gives are the unshakable foundation for us in a world of confusion.
a: Obedience joined with love
True love for the Lord is shown by keeping his commandments. Love is not a feeling but an action.
Rely on the Spirit to teach and remind
In confusion and struggle, the Holy Spirit reminds us of the Lord’s words and leads us out of the fog.
Receive the peace the Lord gives
Even when the world is in turmoil, we can experience a peace that is not shaken by outside circumstances.
q: Do I regularly invite the Holy Spirit to guide my life and decisions?
When I face fear or unease, do I choose to rely on the Lord’s peace?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the Spirit of truth through Jesus, so that I do not walk through life alone. Thank You for giving a peace that passes understanding, reigning in my heart. Please help me to obey Your will in all things, and let the Holy Spirit often remind me of the Lord’s words and guide me on the right path. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: An Open Heart and an Open Home
v: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;
and from there to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony. We were staying some days in this city.
On the Sabbath day we went outside of the city by a riverside, where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and we sat down and spoke to the women who had come together.
A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us. The Lord opened her heart to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.
When she and her household were baptized, she begged us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and stay.” So she persuaded us.
b: On his second missionary journey, Paul came to Philippi in Macedonia, an important Roman city. On the Sabbath they went out of the city to the riverside, looking for a place of prayer, and met a group of women gathered there, to whom they preached the gospel.

Among them was a woman named Lydia, a merchant who sold expensive purple cloth, from the city of Thyatira, a God-fearing woman. The text says, “The Lord opened her heart,” showing that the fruit of the gospel does not depend on persuasive human words; it is God who moves people’s hearts.

Lydia’s response was more than believing and being baptized. She immediately showed it in action: she opened her home and invited Paul and his companions to stay, proving the reality of her faith and her eagerness to serve. It all began with “the Lord opened her heart,” and became the seed for the founding of the church in Philippi.
a: We open our mouths; the Lord opens hearts
Sharing the gospel is our responsibility, but touching hearts is God’s work. Let us share faithfully and pray patiently.
Faith shows itself in action
Lydia did not only hear the word; she responded at once with hospitality, becoming a helper of the gospel work.
An open home becomes a base of blessing
Let our homes, like Lydia’s, become a source of blessing for God’s workers and the church.
q: Am I willing to be someone whose heart the Lord opens, sensitive to God’s calling and guidance?
Does my faith stop at hearing, or have I put it into action to become a blessing to others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Lydia’s story that You are the Lord who opens hearts. Please open my heart too, so that when I hear Your word I not only receive it but take steps of faith. May my life and my home both become vessels of blessing for Your Kingdom. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The King Who Enters the City in Glory
v: As he was now approaching, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,
saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”
He answered them, “I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
b: When Jesus rode a donkey into Jerusalem, his disciples were filled with joy because of the miracles he had done. They praised God and shouted, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” This was not just emotion; it was a testimony of faith. They saw not only Jesus of Nazareth, but the Messiah God had promised, the Prince of Peace.

The Pharisees, however, could not accept this scene, and asked Jesus to silence his disciples. But Jesus’ reply is startling: “If these were silent, the stones would cry out!” When the glorious Lord enters his city, even if people are silent, the earth itself will speak to bear witness to him.

This reminds us that praising the glorious King is not an option; it is a response. If we fall silent because of circumstances, pressure, or fear, God will still raise up witnesses, even making voiceless things speak, to testify to his honor.
a: Boldly witness to the Lord’s glory
Do not be afraid to lift up the name of Jesus before others. He deserves our praise.
Do not let worship fall silent
Even when circumstances seem unsuitable, we can still choose to worship and give thanks.
Value the signs of God’s miracles
Look back on what God has done in our lives, and always keep a heart of joy and praise.
q: Do I often hold back my worship and witness of Jesus because of other people’s opinions?
What has God done that I should praise loudly but have not yet declared?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ, the King of peace, into our lives. Please forgive me for the times I have been silent out of timidity. Increase my faith and courage, so that in any situation I may joyfully praise You and witness for You. May my mouth never be silent, and may my life always proclaim Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Gospel of Faith and the Power of the Gospel
v: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,
requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.
For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;
that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.
Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (and was hindered so far) that I might have some fruit in you also, even as in the rest of the Gentiles.
I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.
So, as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.
For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, for it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes; for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
For in it is revealed a righteousness of God from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.”
b: Paul expresses deep thanks and longing to the church in Rome. He praises their faith, which is known throughout the world, and prays for them without ceasing, hoping that, if God wills, he can visit them in person, share spiritual gifts with them, and strengthen their faith. He longs to be encouraged together with them by their shared faith, and hopes to bear the fruit of the gospel among them.

He feels a deep obligation to share the gospel with everyone, whatever their race, culture, or level of wisdom, and he is eager to preach it with all his strength. He is not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God to save everyone who believes. The gospel reveals God’s righteousness, received not by works but through faith, as it is written, “The righteous shall live by faith.”
a: Boldly proclaim the gospel
Do not be ashamed of the gospel, for it is God’s power to save souls, and the truth the world needs most.
Strengthen one another’s faith
Spiritual fellowship strengthens our faith and lets us comfort and build one another up in the Lord.
Live a life based on faith
Do not rely on works or self-righteousness, but live each day by faith in God’s grace and righteousness.
q: Do I truly believe the gospel is the power of God? Who am I willing to share this gospel with?
Is my life lived from faith to faith, or am I still trying to earn God’s approval by my own effort?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving the gospel of salvation through Jesus Christ, so that I am counted righteous by faith alone and not by works. Please strengthen my faith so that I am not ashamed of the gospel, but boldly proclaim Your power. May I also encourage my brothers and sisters, and grow with them in faith. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: A Covenant of Loyalty and a Choice of Faith
v: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab; for she had heard in the country of Moab how the Lord had visited his people in giving them bread.
She went out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to her mother’s house. May the Lord deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead, and with me.
May the Lord grant you that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices, and wept.
They said to her, “No, but we will go with you to your people.”
Naomi said, “Go back, my daughters. Why will you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
Go back, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, ‘I have hope,’ if I should even have a husband tonight, and should also bear sons,

would you then wait until they were grown? Would you then refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, for it grieves me seriously for your sakes, for the hand of the Lord has gone out against me.”
They lifted up their voice, and wept again; then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth stayed with her.
She said, “Behold, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people, and to her god. Follow your sister-in-law.”
Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. The Lord do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.”
b: After losing her husband and both sons, Naomi, in great sorrow, decided to return to her homeland of Judah, because she had heard that God had visited his people and given them food. She urged her two daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers’ homes and start over, but Ruth chose to go with her, making a deeply moving and resolute declaration: “Your God my God. Where you die, I will die.”

This was not merely family affection, but a turning point of faith. Ruth was choosing not only to follow her mother-in-law, but to make the Lord her God, entrusting her future to a God she had never known firsthand, but whom she had seen in Naomi’s life.

In the midst of great uncertainty, Ruth’s love and trust became a comfort to Naomi and later an important link in the history of salvation. Her choice shows that sincere love and faith always open a new chapter of grace.
a: Choose to trust, however uncertain the future
Even when you cannot see the way ahead, be willing to set out by faith on the journey God has prepared, as Ruth did.
Loyalty and faithfulness bear witness to faith
Holding to love and loyalty in relationships is not only a virtue but the practice of faith.
Let God be the Lord of your life
Do not merely follow people; truly choose, “Your God will be my God,” and resolve to follow the Lord for life.
q: Am I willing, like Ruth, to keep trusting God in loss and hardship?
When I face major decisions, do I depend on how good the circumstances are, or on God’s guidance and presence?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me learn loyalty and faith from Ruth’s life. Even in sorrow and the unknown, You call me to trust You and follow You. Please strengthen my love and commitment in my relationships, and help me not to shrink back or waver. May my life also become part of Your plan of grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Learning Wisdom from Vanity
v: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
Surely oppression makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Better is the end of a thing than the beginning of it. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
b: This passage challenges our instincts about “happiness” and “success.” The Teacher points out that sorrow can be worth more than laughter, because in the hardships of life the heart is more easily touched and more likely to seek true wisdom and transformation.

The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, because loss and suffering force us to face what is real and eternal, while fools seek only escape and pleasure. Hearing a rebuke may be uncomfortable, but it wakes us up more than the entertainment of fools.

The Teacher also says that the end of a matter is better than its beginning, because true fruit and meaning are shown in lasting patience and faithfulness. Anger, bribery, pride, and empty laughter are all vanity and cannot bring eternal value.
a: Look for God’s wisdom in suffering
Do not rush to escape grief, but learn to see God’s light and shaping in it.
Accept rebuke and avoid false entertainment
Choose words that build up life, not things that only make people happy for a moment.
Cultivate patience and humility
Overcome anger and pride, and persevere to the end as an upright person; this is the way of wisdom.
q: When I face suffering or rebuke, am I willing to learn from it, rather than run away or hit back?
Does my heart usually stay in the “house of mirth,” or am I willing to enter the “house of mourning” to seek God’s deeper purpose?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through the Teacher’s words that sorrow and rebuke can also be channels of blessing. Please give me a humble and patient heart, not quick to escape difficulty, but seeking Your wisdom in it. Help me not to be satisfied with empty entertainment, but to find true joy in You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Glorious Path of Self-Denial and Fruitfulness
v: Now there were certain Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
These, therefore, came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
Philip came and told Andrew, and in turn, Andrew came with Philip, and they told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, “The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
He who loves his life will lose it. He who hates his life in this world will keep it to eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me. Where I am, there will my servant also be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this time?’ But for this cause I came to this time.
b: Some Greeks who were not Jews wanted to see Jesus. This request touched something deep in the Lord, who knew that “the time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.” But this glory was not the applause and achievement that people see; it was the road to the cross.

Jesus used the picture of a grain of wheat to explain that unless it falls into the ground and dies, it cannot bear fruit. This was not an abstract lesson, but a truth he was about to live out himself. Death is not the end; it is the beginning of the harvest.

He went on to challenge his disciples: “He who loves his life will lose it.” True life is found in self-denial and service. If we want to follow Jesus, we must imitate his giving of himself and his obedience. Even though his soul was troubled, he still said, “For this cause I came to this time.” This was his acceptance of his mission and his obedience to it.
a: See the value of self-denial
The glory of life is not in protecting ourselves, but in sacrificing and giving ourselves for love, as wheat falls into the ground and bears fruit.
Learn to obey in sorrow
Even when your heart is uneasy, trust that God’s plan is higher than your feelings, and choose to walk steadily in the time God has set.
Glorify God by serving: not just hearing, but following
Those who serve Jesus walk with him and are honored by the Father.
q: Am I willing, like a grain of wheat, to deny myself for God’s Kingdom and bear the fruit of life?
When my heart is troubled, can I still choose to trust God’s arrangement and keep following his will?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus to give his life for us, like a grain of wheat falling into the ground and bearing countless fruits of life. Please help me to understand the value of self-denial, and bravely lay myself down to love, to serve, and to follow You. Even when sorrow comes, I am willing to believe that Your timing is good. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Forgiveness and Hope on the Cross
v: There were also others, two criminals, led with him to be put to death.
When they came to the place that is called The Skull, there they crucified him and the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.
The people stood watching. The rulers with them also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen one!”
The soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, offering him vinegar,
and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!”
An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
One of the criminals who were hanged insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!”
But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Don’t you even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?
And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong.”
He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
Jesus said to him, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”
b: When Jesus was crucified, he faced not only physical pain but also the mockery and scorn of the people, the rulers, and the soldiers. They jeered, “If he is the Christ, let him save himself!” Yet Jesus’ reply was one of great love and forgiveness: “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”

Of the two criminals beside him, one kept scoffing, but the other, at the edge of death, woke up. He admitted his guilt, recognized Jesus’ innocence and holiness, and said with simple faith, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.” This faint but sincere cry brought Jesus’ most tender promise: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.”
This is the height of grace: even on the cross, Jesus embraced the one who repented with love.
a: Jesus’ forgiveness has no limit
No matter how great our wrong, if we repent and turn back, Jesus is willing to forgive and receive us.
Respond to the Lord’s grace with faith
Salvation does not come by knowledge or good deeds, but by simply confessing sin, believing, and calling on the Lord’s name.
Choose mercy even in pain
Even in the most extreme suffering, Jesus chose to forgive and love, and we should follow his example.
q: Am I still carrying unrepented sin and hiding from Jesus’ forgiveness?
When others offend me, am I willing to choose forgiveness as Jesus did?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing Your boundless love on the cross. Even in the deepest suffering, Jesus interceded for others and answered the prayer of the repentant. Please forgive my sins, so that like the repentant criminal I may simply trust in You. Teach me to learn from Your forgiveness and to live a life of mercy and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Turn from Shame to Glory
v: They will build the old wastes, they will raise up the former desolations, and they will repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and your vinedressers.
But you will be named the Priests of the Lord. They will call you the Ministers of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will boast in their glory.
Instead of your shame you will have double; and instead of dishonor they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them.
For I, the Lord, love justice. I hate robbery with iniquity. I will give them their recompense in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed.”

I will greatly rejoice in the Lord. My soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

For as the earth brings forth its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth, so the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.
They will build the old wastes, they will raise up the former desolations, and they will repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and your vinedressers.
But you will be named the Priests of the Lord. They will call you the Ministers of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will boast in their glory.
Instead of your shame you will have double; and instead of dishonor they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them.
For I, the Lord, love justice. I hate robbery with iniquity. I will give them their recompense in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed.”

I will greatly rejoice in the Lord. My soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

For as the earth brings forth its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth, so the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.
b: This passage continues the promise of the Messiah’s year of jubilee, describing God’s restoration and reversal for his people. Those who once lived in ruins will rebuild the wastes with their own hands, and those who were put to shame will receive a double inheritance and joy. God does not only heal the wounds of the past; he gives honor and identity. His people will be called “the Priests of the Lord” and “the Ministers of our God,” and will be recognized among all peoples as a blessed offspring.

All of these promises rest on God’s justice and truth. He loves justice, hates iniquity, and personally makes an everlasting covenant with his people. In the end, the people clothed in the robe of righteousness and the garments of salvation will, like seeds sprouting in a garden, cause righteousness and praise to spring up among all nations, glorifying the Lord’s name.
a: Believe God can turn your hardship around
However much shame and desolation you have been through, God can rebuild every ruin in your life.
Live out your identity as a priest
We are called to be God’s servants, living lives of holiness and service that bear witness to his glory.
Respond to grace with joy
Because God has equipped us with salvation and righteousness, let us respond to his grace with praise and thanksgiving.
q: Are there “ruins” in my life that need God to rebuild and restore?
Am I living out my identity as a servant of God, becoming a vessel that blesses others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for working a turnaround in my life, lifting me out of shame and giving me Your glory and honor. Please help me remember that I am Your priest, to shine for You in the world. May my life become a garden of praise to You, bearing witness among all peoples to Your righteousness and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Jesus Is Lord and Christ
v: “Brothers, I may tell you freely of the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
Therefore, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that of the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, he would raise up the Christ to sit on his throne,
he foreseeing this spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul wasn’t left in Hades, neither did his flesh see decay.
This Jesus God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses.
Being therefore exalted by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this which you now see and hear.
For David didn’t ascend into the heavens, but he says himself, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit by my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
“Let all the house of Israel therefore know certainly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”
b: In his sermon at Pentecost, Peter quoted David’s psalm to show plainly that Jesus is the Messiah God promised. David, though king and prophet, admitted that he too was waiting for the descendant who would sit on the throne. He foresaw the resurrection of Christ, saying that his soul would not be left in Hades and his body would not see decay.

Jesus rose from the dead, and the disciples became witnesses of this resurrection glory. He is now seated at the right hand of the Father, has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, and has poured him out on those who believe, so that the Kingdom of God advances through the Spirit’s power. Peter closed with a firm declaration: God has made Jesus both Lord and Christ.
a: Firmly believe that Jesus is Lord
He is not a teacher of the past, but the Lord whom God appointed, a living Savior and King.
Proclaim the gospel of the resurrection
Like the disciples, we are called to be witnesses of Jesus’ resurrection and to bring this hope to more people.
Rely on the Spirit to live out your witness
Jesus has poured out the promised Holy Spirit, so we depend on the Spirit to live as disciples of Christ.
q: Do I truly acknowledge Jesus as the Lord of my life, and not only agree with it in my mind?
Am I willing to witness boldly for Jesus and share his resurrection and grace?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for making Jesus both Lord and Christ, so that I no longer live in sin or in fear of death. I confess him as the Lord of my life, trust in his resurrection, and rely on the Holy Spirit to witness for him. May my life glorify You and proclaim Your Kingdom to the ends of the earth. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Godliness That Is the Same Inside and Out
v: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But these you ought to have done, and not to have left the other undone.
You blind guides, who strain out a gnat and swallow a camel!
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and self-indulgence.
You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that the outside of it may become clean also.”
b: In this passage Jesus sharply rebukes the hypocritical scribes and Pharisees. They were extremely careful about religious details, even tithing their mint, dill, and cumin, yet they neglected the heart of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. They put so much weight on outward ritual that they overlooked inward obedience to God and compassion for others.

Jesus used a vivid picture to expose their absurdity: “You strain out a gnat and swallow a camel.” These religious leaders cared only about surface cleanliness while allowing greed and corruption to fill their hearts. The Lord calls them, and us, to cleanse the inside first, so that inside and out we may be holy before God.
a: Value the heart over appearance
Faith is not for show; it begins in the heart, with true reverence for God and love for your neighbor.
Hold fast to justice, mercy, and faithfulness
While pursuing the details of spiritual life, do not neglect the core of love.
Beware the trap of false piety
Do not merely polish an outward “spiritual look,” but let God shine on the true motives deep in your heart.
q: In my life of faith, do I focus too much on outward form and neglect inward reality?
Am I willing to let God cleanse my heart, so that my words and actions are consistent and I live out justice and love?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, please shine Your light on me and show me whether I am living in outward piety while losing my love for You and compassion for others. Help me not merely to perform religious rituals, but to truly live out justice, mercy, and faithfulness. May I be clean inside and out, and please You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Remove the Hardness of Heart and Live God’s Love
v: Behold, to Yahweh your God belongs heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is therein.
Only Yahweh set his affection on your fathers to love them, and he chose their offspring after them, even you above all peoples, as it is today.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked.
For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes bribes.
He executes justice for the fatherless and widow, and loves the foreigner, in giving him food and clothing.
Therefore love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
b: In these words Moses calls Israel to recognize God’s greatness and his choosing. Heaven and earth and everything in them belong to the Lord, yet he set his love in a special way on their fathers and chose their descendants from among all peoples to be his own. This was not because of anything they had earned, but because of God’s gracious choice and loving-kindness.

So Moses tells the people to “circumcise the foreskin of your heart” and to stop being stiff-necked. God does not look at outward religiousness; he values a heart that is repentant and tender. He is the greatest of all, yet he personally defends the fatherless and the widow and provides for the foreigner. Since he has such compassion for people, he asks his people to follow his example and love others, especially the vulnerable foreigner living among them.
a: Remove the hardness and impurity in your heart
Don’t merely keep outward rules, but be willing to let God turn your heart around and take away rebellion and self-righteousness.
Imitate God’s acts of love
The God we revere delights in showing mercy and justice; we too should help the lonely and the suffering in practical ways.
Remember your own weak beginnings
When we remember that we too have known God’s grace in the wilderness, in exile and in need, we should learn to have compassion on others.
q: Am I willing to let God deal with the pride and hardness hidden in my heart?
Who are the “foreigners” in my life whom I can reach out to and show mercy?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that although You own everything, You chose me, loved me and called me to live out Your purposes. Cleanse the hardness and impurity from my heart, and make me gentle and humble, willing to care for others. Help me follow Your compassion and become a vessel of Your love in this world. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: A Forgiving Heart and the Standard of the Kingdom
v: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”
Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but until seventy times seven.
Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is likened to a certain king, who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
When he had begun to reckon, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
The servant therefore fell down and kneeled before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’
The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.
“But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him, and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’
He would not, but went and cast him into prison, until he should pay back that which was due.
So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told to their lord all that was done.
Then his lord called him in, and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.
Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’
His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him.
So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”
b: Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive a brother who sins against him. He thought seven times was already generous, but Jesus answered, “seventy times seven.” He was not setting a number; he was showing that forgiveness should have no limit.

Jesus explained this truth with a parable. A servant owed his master an enormous sum he could never repay, yet the master had compassion and cancelled the entire debt. But that servant turned around and seized a fellow servant who owed him a small amount, and showed no mercy at all. When the master heard of it, he rebuked him for his ingratitude and handed him over to the jailers until the debt was paid.

Jesus concluded that if we do not forgive others from the heart, we cannot truly receive forgiveness from our Heavenly Father. The standard of the Kingdom is not revenge, and not mere fairness, but grace and forgiveness.
a: Forgive others from the heart
True forgiveness is not just words on the lips; it releases the other person from the heart, and releases yourself as well.
Remember the grace you have received
What we owe God is far greater than what anyone owes us. Having been forgiven so much, we should treat others with kindness.
Build a Kingdom heart
The Kingdom does not run on law and calculation, but on living out God’s character: compassion, forgiveness and mercy.
q: Am I still holding on to someone’s offense and refusing to let go?
Do I often forget that I too have been unconditionally forgiven by God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, You have forgiven me with limitless grace and given me freedom and peace. Give me a soft heart, so that I may learn to forgive others from the heart, no longer keeping count of their offenses, but living out the culture of Your Kingdom’s grace. Help me remember that I too am a forgiven person, and treat those around me with the same compassion. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: True Repentance and the Path of Blessing
v: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
Whoever causes the upright to go astray in an evil way will fall into his own trap, but the blameless will inherit good.
The rich man is wise in his own eyes, but the poor who has understanding sees through him.
When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
b: These proverbs sharply contrast the attitude and outcome of the righteous and the wicked. The passage first warns us: “He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.” If we refuse to hear God’s word, our relationship with him is cut off, and even our prayers are not accepted.

Next we are told that those who plot against the upright will fall into their own trap, while the blameless receive blessing under God’s keeping. A person who trusts only in wealth and thinks himself wise is proud in a false way, but a person with real spiritual insight, even if poor, can see through the pretense.

The most precious word here is verse 13: “He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.” This is a spiritual law. What God wants is not outward piety, but a heart of sincere repentance.
a: Not only pray, but obey
Prayer without listening to God’s word and obeying it loses its power. Let us return to God and first listen to his voice.
Face your sin honestly
Covering up only takes us further from God. Only honest confession and repentance lead to mercy and release.
Live out true wisdom
Wisdom is measured not by wealth or position, but by whether we fear God and turn away from evil.
q: Am I drawing near to God only with my lips, without sincerely obeying his word?
Am I hiding some sin, while God is calling me to confess it to him and turn back?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, what You value is my honest, repentant heart, not a false piety. Shine Your light on me and show me the dark corners of my life I have not yet surrendered to You. Help me stop covering my sin, and instead confess it and forsake it with courage, so that I may enter Your abundant mercy and blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Wisdom and Joy as We Grow Through Trials
v: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion: Greetings.
Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,
knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven by the wind and tossed.
Let not that man think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
But let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;
and the rich, in that he is made low, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.
For the sun arose with the scorching wind, and withered the grass; and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. So the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to those who love him.
b: James writes to the scattered twelve tribes and begins by encouraging believers: when you face trials of every kind, count it all joy. This is not positive thinking that runs from reality; it is a truth of spiritual life. Trials train our faith, and the endurance they produce makes us more mature and complete.

He reminds us that when we lack wisdom in hard times, we can ask the God who gives generously; he is glad to give us guidance and light. But we must ask in faith, without doubting or wavering, or we are like waves of the sea, tossed about and unable to receive God’s abundance.

He also points out that whether our station is humble or wealthy does not change our worth before God. The lowly can rejoice in being lifted up in the Lord; the rich should find honor in humility, because all this will pass away like a flower in the grass.
Finally he promises a beautiful ending: whoever endures temptation and stands the test will receive the crown of life from the Lord, a reward for all who love him.
a: Hold on to faith in trials
Suffering is not a stumbling block but a springboard for growth. Let us see trials as tools God uses to shape us.
Ask for wisdom without doubting
When we face difficulties, we don’t grit our teeth and manage alone; we ask God for wisdom in faith, and he gladly guides our path.
Value what is eternal
Whether rich or poor in this life, what matters is not our position but whether we love the Lord and trust him to the end.
q: Do I easily lose heart in trials, forgetting that God is refining my life?
Do I ask for wisdom with simple faith, or do I let doubt cloud my thoughts and heart?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for helping me understand that suffering is not Your abandonment but Your shaping. Give me wisdom, and teach me to see Your hand in every trial, to stand firm by faith, and to receive the crown that never fades. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Be Strong and Courageous: Entering the Promised Land
v: Now after the death of Moses the servant of Yahweh, Yahweh spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ servant, saying,
“Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, you, and all this people, to the land which I give to them, even to the children of Israel.
I have given you every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, as I told Moses.
From the wilderness and this Lebanon even to the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your border.
No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.
Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go.

This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid, neither be dismayed: for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”
b: After Moses’ death, Israel faced a new leader and a new journey. When God said to Joshua, “Arise,” he was not telling him to imitate Moses, but to take up a new mission with courage. Moses’ era had ended, but God’s promise had not: he would give them the land flowing with milk and honey, and would be with Joshua just as he had been with Moses.

More than once God told Joshua to “be strong and courageous,” because ahead lay territory he had never walked, and it would take courage and, even more, faith. That faith rests on God’s presence and God’s word.

God stressed: “This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night.” True strength does not come from personality or training, but from rooting ourselves in God’s word and obeying it. When we build on God’s truth, we will succeed wherever we go.
a: Rely on God’s promises in times of change
Life brings seasons of transition, changes of role and new challenges, but God’s presence and promises never change.
Practice strong faith
Being strong does not mean suppressing fear; it means choosing to trust God and walk in his way even while afraid.
Meditate on God’s word day and night
Store God’s word in your heart, reflect on it daily and declare it with your mouth, and you will have strength to face every new challenge.
q: When I face a new challenge or responsibility, do I become afraid and stand still?
Do I treat God’s word as my daily source of strength, meditating on it day and night and putting it into practice?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You will never leave me nor forsake me. When I face the unknown, give me a strong and courageous heart, help me remember Your promises and trust You firmly. May I meditate on Your word day and night and walk in Your will, receiving the abundance and peace You give. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Looking to the Loving Lord in Distress
v: Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.
My soul still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.
It is of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
“Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
b: As the prophet Jeremiah thought about the suffering of a fallen nation and a ruined home, his heart was bowed down within him, close to despair. He described his misery as wormwood and gall, bitter to the very bones. Yet in the midst of that painful memory, his heart turned to one truth: “This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.”

This hope did not come from a change of circumstances, but from the character of God: his loving kindness never ceases, and his compassion never fails. Every morning is new, and his faithfulness is great beyond measure. In the ruins of despair he held on to God’s faithfulness and declared, “Yahweh is my portion; therefore I will hope in him.”
Waiting for God’s salvation may be long, but it is a blessed path. For all who wait for him and seek him will experience his grace and deliverance.
a: Turn your distress into prayer
When suffering and pressure come, don’t suppress them or run from them; bring all your honest emotions to God and pour them out.
Renew your hope every morning
However hard yesterday was, God’s love and compassion are new today, and fresh grace arrives every morning.
Wait quietly for God to act
Faith is not frantic activity but quiet trust. Even when you can’t see a way out, believe that his salvation will come.
q: When I face hardship and distress, am I willing to stop and reflect on God’s love and compassion?
Have I learned to wait quietly for God’s salvation, rather than rushing to find a human solution?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, when my heart is full of sorrow and bitterness, remind me that Your loving kindness never ends and Your compassion is new every morning. May I still choose to look to You in the dark, and still trust Your salvation as I wait. Give me a quiet heart that learns to wait for Your work. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: A Diligent Life and Perseverance in Doing Good
v: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks in rebellion and not after the tradition which they received from us.
For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us. For we didn’t behave ourselves rebelliously among you,
neither did we eat bread from anyone’s hand without paying for it, but in labor and travail worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you;
not because we don’t have the right, but to make ourselves an example to you, that you should imitate us.
For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: that if anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat.
For we hear of some who walk among you in rebellion, who don’t work at all, but are busybodies.
Now those who are that way, we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ that they work with quietness, and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing well.
b: Paul solemnly tells believers to keep away from those who live in disorder, who are unwilling to work and who only meddle in other people’s affairs. He reminds the church that life in the Lord should be a witness, and a disciple’s life should show godliness and responsibility in daily living.

He uses himself as an example. Though an apostle has authority, he chose to work with his own hands so as not to burden the brothers and sisters, and to show others how to live a fitting life. Faith is not godliness displayed only at meetings; it bears witness to Christ in everyday work and life.

Paul especially says, “If anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat.” This stresses responsibility and shows that faith must connect with real life. If our faith is not accompanied by action, it becomes empty talk.
Finally he encourages believers: whatever the circumstances, do not lose heart because of difficulties or the influence of others. Persevere in doing good and live a life that pleases God.
a: Learn the attitude of working for the Lord
Even though we have grace, we should put real effort into daily life, not depending on others but doing work that pleases God.
Witness through practice
Faith cannot be only spoken piety; we bear witness to the Lord’s glory through earnest living and loving service.
Keep doing good without growing weary
Even when others don’t understand or cooperate, remember that the Lord values every good deed we do for him.
q: Is my way of life one that others can imitate?
When I feel tired, am I still willing to lean on the Lord’s grace and keep doing good without losing heart?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me that faith is not empty talk but godliness lived out each day. Give me a diligent and enduring heart, that I may not take laziness for comfort or lose heart in difficulty. May my life bear witness to Your truth and glory as I do good. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Eyes of Faith and the Report of Fear
v: They went and came to Moses, and to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word to them, and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told him, and said, “We came to the land where you sent us; and surely it flows with milk and honey; and this is its fruit.
However the people are strong who dwell in the land, and the cities are fortified, and very great. Moreover, we saw the children of Anak there.
Amalek dwells in the land of the South. The Hittite, the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwell in the hill country. The Canaanite dwells by the sea, and along the side of the Jordan.”
Caleb quieted the people before Moses, and said, “Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.”
But the men who went up with him said, “We aren’t able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.”

They brought up an evil report of the land which they had spied out to the children of Israel, saying, “The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that eats up its inhabitants; and all the people whom we saw in it are men of great stature.
There we saw the Nephilim, the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. We were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”
