b: After Moses sent spies to explore Canaan, they reported that the land truly flowed with milk and honey, a picture of the promised land. But although they had seen with their own eyes how rich God’s promise was, ten of the spies were frightened by the difficulties. They saw only towering enemies and fortified cities, and they began to spread fear, saying they felt as small as grasshoppers.

Caleb, by contrast, showed faith. He urged the people to go up at once and take the land, because he believed God’s leading was far greater than the strength of their enemies. This contrast shows that faith and fear do not come from circumstances, but from how the heart sees God.

True faith keeps believing God’s promise in the midst of challenges and keeps stepping forward bravely before giants. As Caleb said, “We are well able to overcome it,” because the key to victory is not how strong we are, but whether God is with us.
a: See the promise and don’t be scared off by difficulty
Spiritual vision rises above circumstances and focuses on God’s faithfulness, not the size of the problem.
Reject negative voices
The world frightens faith with the word “impossible,” but faith does not ignore reality; it chooses to believe God’s word within reality.
Follow Caleb’s faith
Even if you are in the minority, speak up bravely and encourage others to believe God’s promise, so that together you can enter the land of victory.
q: When I face a challenge, do I first see the difficulty, or do I first remember God’s promise?
Like Caleb, am I willing to hold on to my declaration of faith when everyone else is afraid?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing an abundant promised land for me. Help me not to be frightened by difficulties, nor to follow the crowd in believing negative voices. Let me, like Caleb, have a simple and courageous faith, moving forward by Your word and receiving the inheritance You give. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: A Life Surrounded by Loving Kindness
v: For this, let everyone who is godly pray to you in a time when you may be found. Surely when the great waters overflow, they shall not reach to him.
You are my hiding place. You will preserve me from trouble. You will surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah.
I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.
Don’t be like the horse, or like the mule, which have no understanding, who must be controlled with bit and bridle, or else they will not come near to you.
Many sorrows come to the wicked, but loving kindness shall surround him who trusts in Yahweh.
Be glad in Yahweh, and rejoice, you righteous! Shout for joy, all you who are upright in heart!
b: In this psalm David reminds us to draw near to God and pray to him while he may be found. When the great waters overflow, it will be too late. Only those who seek God early are kept in times of trouble and not swept away.

God is not only our hiding place; he is also the teacher who shows us the way to go. He does not want us to be like a senseless mule that has to be forced forward, but to follow his leading with willing hearts and walk the road he has prepared for us.

Those who trust in God will still face challenges, but loving kindness surrounds them, while those who oppose God will have many sorrows. So the righteous should be glad in the Lord, because what we have is not only the peace of forgiven sin but also his constant presence and a song of deliverance that goes with us.
a: Seize the opportunity to draw near to God
Don’t wait until trouble arrives to seek God. Build a habit of prayer in times of peace, and keep your heart aligned with the Lord.
Learn a teachable heart
God wants to teach us himself to walk the right path, not by pressure, but because we trust him and love him and are willing to obey.
Keep a heart of thanks and joy
Even when circumstances are hard, we can shout for joy because we know God’s loving kindness surrounds us.
q: Am I willing to draw near to God and listen to his guidance while he may be found?
Am I willing to be like a gentle sheep who hears the shepherd’s voice, or like a mule that must be forced to move?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You are my hiding place, and that when I seek You, You surround me with loving kindness. Give me a soft and obedient heart, so that I am willing to listen to Your word and walk the way You show me. Even when the storms come, may my heart be glad, because I know You are with me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Meeting God in the Still Small Voice
v: He arose, and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the Mount of God.
He came there to a cave, and lodged there; and behold, the word of Yahweh came to him, and he said to him, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

He said, “I have been very jealous for Yahweh, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.”

He said, “Go out, and stand on the mountain before Yahweh.” Behold, Yahweh passed by, and a great and strong wind tore the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before Yahweh; but Yahweh was not in the wind; and after the wind an earthquake; but Yahweh was not in the earthquake;
and after the earthquake a fire; but Yahweh was not in the fire; and after the fire a still small voice.
It was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entrance of the cave. Behold, a voice came to him, and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

He said, “I have been very jealous for Yahweh, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.”
b: Utterly exhausted and afraid, Elijah fled to Horeb, the mountain of God. He walked forty days and nights on the strength of the food God provided, a sign that God personally sustains us even in desperate times.

Hiding in a cave, Elijah poured out to God his feelings of loneliness and helplessness, and of zeal that seemed to have borne no fruit. He saw Israel abandon God, and he was heartbroken and sorrowful, feeling he was fighting alone with his life at stake.

God did not appear in the mighty wind, the earthquake or the fire, but came in a still, small voice. This reveals deeply that God’s work is not always dramatic; sometimes he touches our souls most deeply in the quietest and smallest moments.

When Elijah heard the gentle voice, he covered his face and came out, an act of reverence before the holy presence and a response to God’s renewed calling. God did not rebuke him for his weakness; he spoke with him gently and gave him a new mission again.
a: Look for God in the quiet
Don’t expect God to work only in great and spectacular events; learn to listen for his voice in what is small and quiet.
Keep reverence and trust toward God
Even when you feel alone or defeated, believe that God is still in control and has not left us.
Accept renewal and sending
When you are weary, don’t stay in self-pity, but open your heart to receive God’s fresh calling and direction.
q: When I am tired and discouraged, am I willing to stop and seek God’s comfort and guidance in his still small voice?
Am I willing to let God send me out again, even if the circumstances are still hard?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, when I am weary, lonely and lost, quiet my heart so that I may meet You in Your small and gentle voice. Teach me to hear Your word after the storm and to sense Your presence in the stillness. Strengthen me and send me out again, so that I may keep going in Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Witnessing with Hope and Gentleness
v: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts; and always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear:
having a good conscience; that, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disciplined who curse your good way of life in Christ.
b: The apostle Peter teaches believers that in any circumstance we should set apart Christ as Lord in our hearts, putting him first in our lives. When someone asks why we have such hope, we should always be ready to answer with gentleness and reverence, not with arguing or pride.

Believers must also keep a clear conscience and live out the character of Christ. Even when we are slandered or misunderstood, our good conduct in Christ will in the end make those who accuse us ashamed, and bear witness to God’s glory.
a: Always be ready to share the hope in you
In good times and bad, be prepared to share the hope of your faith with others in a gentle and reverent way.
Respond with gentleness and reverence
Witnessing to Christ is not only explaining doctrine, but responding with humility, respect and love, reflecting the Lord’s character.
Live with a clear conscience
Hold to honesty and integrity in conduct and character, so that your life itself becomes a powerful witness.
q: When someone asks about my faith, can I express the hope in my heart gently and firmly?
Does my conduct let the people around me see Christ in my character?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for placing an eternal hope in my heart. Teach me to be ready at all times to answer people gently and reverently, to live with a clear conscience, and to glorify Your name. May my life be a witness to Your grace and draw people to know You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Let Christ Be Proclaimed, Whatever the Circumstances
v: Now I desire to have you know, brothers, that the things which happened to me have turned out rather to the progress of the Good News;
so that it became evident to the whole praetorian guard, and to all the rest, that my bonds are in Christ;
and that most of the brothers in the Lord, being made confident by my bonds, are more abundantly bold to speak the word of God without fear.
Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and strife, and some also out of good will.
The former insincerely preach Christ from selfish ambition, thinking that they add affliction to my chains;
but the latter out of love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the Good News.
What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed. I rejoice in this, yes, and will rejoice.
b: Writing from prison, Paul tells believers that everything that has happened to him has not hindered the gospel but has actually advanced it. His chains made Christ known to the whole palace guard and to many others, and encouraged the brothers and sisters to have more faith and courage in proclaiming God’s word.

Even though some preach Christ out of envy and strife, or from impure motives, Paul cares about one thing: whatever the motive, Christ is proclaimed! So he chooses to rejoice, and to go on rejoicing. Paul’s largeness of heart and focus remind us that what truly matters is that Christ be glorified.
a: Accept that suffering can advance the gospel
Sometimes the hardships we go through are the very way God makes the gospel flourish.
Focus on Christ being lifted high
Whatever people’s motives, what matters most is that Christ’s name is proclaimed. Let us not stumble over what people do, but fix our eyes on Christ alone.
Keep a joyful attitude
In every circumstance, choose Christ as the source of your joy, and let the steadfastness and hope that come from God show in your life.
q: When I meet unfairness or hardship, can I still see God’s purpose in it?
Are my eyes on what people do, or on Christ being lifted high?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that the gospel is not hindered even in hard times. Give me a heart like Paul’s, so that whatever my circumstances, I take Christ as my joy and hope. Help me look beyond people’s motives and see Your wonderful work, and be willing in every situation to proclaim Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Life and Joy in God’s Presence
v: (A Miktam of David.) Preserve me, God, for in you do I take refuge.
My soul, you have said to Yahweh, “You are my Lord. Apart from you I have no good thing.”
As for the saints who are in the earth, they are the excellent ones in whom is all my delight.
Their sorrows shall be multiplied who give gifts to another god. Their drink offerings of blood I will not offer, nor take their names on my lips.
Yahweh assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure.
The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.
I will bless Yahweh, who has given me counsel. Yes, my heart instructs me in the night seasons.
I have set Yahweh always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be shaken.
Therefore my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also dwell in safety.
For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.
You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
b: In this psalm David expresses a deep trust in God and joy in him. He declares that God is his everything: his inheritance, his good, his keeping and his joy. Even when those around him choose other gods, he stays single-hearted toward the Lord, because he knows that apart from God there is no real blessing.

Because David keeps God always before him, his heart is steady, he is instructed in the night, and he walks the right path by day. He is sure that God will not abandon him, will show him the path of life, and that in God’s presence he will find fullness of joy and eternal pleasures.
a: Trust in God alone
In a changing and restless world, choose to rely on no other security, but trust in God alone and treasure him as the most precious inheritance of your life.
Stay alert to God and revere him
Day and night, keep God before you, and let his word guide your thoughts and actions as you live a life walking with him.
Pursue real joy in God’s presence
Worldly pleasures are brief; only satisfaction in God’s presence lasts forever. Build your longing and contentment on your relationship with God.
q: Is my heart really convinced that God is the greatest good in my life?
In daily life, do I consciously keep God before me and let him guide me?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, You are the inheritance of my life, and all my good is found in You. Help me to meditate on Your word day and night, to trust in You firmly, and to find fullness of joy in Your presence. May my life always walk with You and enjoy pleasures forever at Your right hand. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Repentance Brings Restoration
v: Yahweh spoke to Manasseh, and to his people; but they didn’t listen.
Therefore Yahweh brought on them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh in chains, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
When he was in distress, he begged Yahweh his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
He prayed to him; and he was entreated by him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that Yahweh he was God.

Now after this he built an outer wall to the city of David, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entrance at the fish gate; and he compassed Ophel about with it, and raised it up to a very great height; and he put captains of the army in all the fortified cities of Judah.
He took away the foreign gods, and the idol out of the house of Yahweh, and all the altars that he had built in the mountain of the house of Yahweh, and in Jerusalem, and cast them out of the city.
He built up the altar of Yahweh, and sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and of thanksgiving, and commanded Judah to serve Yahweh, the God of Israel.
Nevertheless the people still sacrificed in the high places, but only to Yahweh their God.
b: Manasseh rebelled against God, led the people into evil and ignored God’s warning, and in the end he fell into the hands of the king of Assyria, was bound with hooks and chains, and taken to Babylon to suffer. Yet in his distress he begged the Lord and humbled himself greatly before him. God heard his prayer and brought him back to Jerusalem to his throne.

After experiencing God’s mercy, Manasseh showed repentance in action: he tore down the idols, rebuilt the altar, offered peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded the people to worship the one true God. Although the people still sacrificed at the high places, their direction had turned toward the Lord.
This passage shows us that no matter how rebellious our past, if we repent sincerely, God is always merciful, listens and restores us.
a: Repent humbly in hard times
When trouble comes, don’t complain or harden your heart, but like Manasseh humble yourself before God and seek his rescue.
Repentance needs action
True repentance is not only confessing sin with the mouth, but removing the idols in the heart, renewing the direction of life and rebuilding our relationship with God.
Give your worship to God
Even in the process of correction, give all your worship to the Lord alone, and let nothing take his place.
q: When I run into trouble, do I run from God, or turn to him and seek him?
Is there still an “idol” in my life that needs to be removed, or some area that has drifted from God’s will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your abundant love and mercy; even though I have wandered far from You, You are still willing to hear my repentance and my cry. Help me remove every idol from my heart and set my will again to worship You, so that my life may be renewed and revived through You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Humility Brings True Honor
v: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, saying to them,
“When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.

But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have glory in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
b: After watching the guests scramble for the best seats, Jesus taught them with a parable: don’t exalt yourself by taking the seat of honor, or you may be asked to move and be shamed. It is better to sit humbly in the lowest place and let the host himself invite you up, and then you will be honored before everyone.

Jesus pointed out a spiritual principle: everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted. What God values is a humble heart that honors him as great, not a struggle for status before others.
This teaching reminds us that on every occasion and in every service we should humble ourselves, and let God lift us up in his own time and way.
a: Learn humility in attitude
Don’t fight for position or think yourself important; quietly wait for God’s arrangement and promotion.
Hand over the right to glory to God
Don’t seek the approval of people; trust God’s eyes and timing, and let him personally bear witness for us.
Respect others and give way to one another
In a group, learn to honor and appreciate others instead of centering on yourself. This is humility in practice.
q: Have I, consciously or unconsciously, wanted to gain status and respect before others?
Am I willing to entrust my place and my glory to God and quietly wait for him to lift me up?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, give me a humble heart. Let me not strive in my own effort for glory, but look to You alone and let You lead my way. May I be humble in the eyes of people and honored in Your eyes. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Honor Through the Grace of a Covenant
v: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”
There was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David; and the king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” He said, “I am your servant.”
The king said, “Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him?” Ziba said to the king, “Jonathan has yet a son, who is lame in his feet.”
The king said to him, “Where is he?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.”
Then King David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.
Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, and fell on his face, and did obeisance. David said, “Mephibosheth?” He answered, “Behold, your servant!”

David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father; and you shall eat bread at my table continually.”
He bowed down, and said, “What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?”
Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said to him, “All that pertained to Saul and to all his house, I have given to your master’s son.

You shall till the land for him, you, and your sons, and your servants; and you shall bring in the fruits, that your master’s son may have bread to eat; but Mephibosheth your master’s son shall eat bread always at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
b: David remembered his covenant with Jonathan and took the initiative to look for anyone left of Saul’s house to show them kindness. When he learned that Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, David at once brought him to the palace, restored the land of his grandfather Saul, and let him eat at his own table continually.

Mephibosheth considered himself nothing but a “dead dog,” yet he received great grace from David, with honor and provision. This is a picture of God’s grace: we did not deserve it, but because of the love between Jesus Christ and the Father, we are invited to become members of God’s household and to enjoy eternal blessing.
a: Remember the new covenant God has made with us
Just as David remembered his covenant with Jonathan, we should always give thanks and remember the covenant of grace God made with us through Christ.
Treat others with grace
As God has freely shown grace to us, we should treat others with mercy and kindness, especially the weak and helpless.
Dine with the Lord and live in your honored identity
Mephibosheth ate continually at the king’s table; we too should draw near to the Lord every day and live out the dignity and gratitude of called children.
q: Do I truly recognize that I did not deserve it, yet received grace because of Christ?
Because I have received God’s grace, do I also show kindness to others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for making an unchanging covenant of grace with me through Jesus Christ. Though I did not deserve it, You received me in love and honored me. Help me live out this grace and bring Your love and mercy to those around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Be Strengthened in the Love of Christ
v: For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man;
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strong to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us,
to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
b: Paul bows his knees in prayer for believers, asking the Father, according to the riches of his glory, to strengthen our inner being through the Holy Spirit, so that Christ may dwell in our hearts through faith. When Christ is the center of our lives, our love can be deeply rooted and our lives can grow steady.

Paul also hopes that believers, together with all the saints, will know the breadth, length, height and depth of Christ’s love that surpasses understanding, and be filled with all the fullness of God. This love and power are far beyond our imagination, because God works within us and is able to do more than we ask or think, so that he is glorified in the church and in Christ forever.
a: Pray for God to strengthen your heart
When you are in difficulty or weakness, don’t grit your teeth and manage on your own, but kneel humbly and ask the Holy Spirit to add strength to your inner being.
Be rooted in Christ’s love
Only by deeply experiencing Christ’s love can our faith and love stand firm and not be shaken by circumstances.
Believe God can do more than you ask or think
Don’t limit what God does; look to him in faith and believe he can do wonderful things in your life.
q: When I feel tired and weak, do I know to turn to the Holy Spirit for strength?
Is my heart truly filled with Christ’s love? Do I believe God can do more in my life than I ask or think?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for strengthening my heart through the Holy Spirit and filling me with the love of Christ. Help me be rooted in Your love and trust in Your limitless power, so that my life continually bears witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Learning to Praise in Sorrow
v: Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben (that is, See, a son). For she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction. For now my husband will love me.”
She conceived again, and bore a son; and said, “Because Yahweh has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon (that is, Hearing).
She conceived again, and bore a son; and said, “Now this time will my husband be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi (that is, Joined).
She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time I will praise Yahweh.” Therefore she named him Judah (that is, Praise). Then she stopped bearing.
b: Leah lived in a marriage where she was unloved, carrying the pain of being overlooked. But the Lord saw her suffering, had compassion on her, and enabled her to bear sons. With each birth Leah’s feelings gradually changed: from hoping to win her husband’s love through her sons, to finally turning her focus to the Lord and praising him.

The birth of Judah marked a breakthrough in Leah’s faith. She no longer clung to human acceptance, but found her joy in God alone. However people treat us, God’s eyes are always on us; he hears, sympathizes and gives grace, so that even in sorrow we can learn to praise.
a: Believe God hears your sorrow
Even when people seem to overlook us, God still sees us and has compassion on us. He is a help at all times.
Turn from human expectations to God
Don’t rest the worth of your life on people; fix your eyes on God and seek his approval and love.
Learn to praise in suffering
Even in hard circumstances, learn to praise God, because praise frees the heart from bitterness and turns it toward freedom and joy.
q: When I feel overlooked or unloved, do I remember that God still watches over me?
Is my heart willing to be released from human expectations and seek God’s pleasure alone?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You listen to my cry even when I am most lonely and overlooked. Help me not to place my hope in people, but to look to You alone. Even in difficulty, may I, like Leah, learn to praise You and rejoice in Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Helping a Brother in Love
v: “‘If your brother has become poor, and his hand can’t support him among you, then you shall uphold him: as a foreigner and a tenant he shall live with you.
Take no interest from him or profit, but fear your God; that your brother may live among you.
You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.
I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.’”
b: God taught Israel that when a brother among them became poor and fell into hardship, they must not stand by and let him perish, much less take advantage of him for profit. Instead they were to help him in love, accepting and supporting him as they would a foreigner living among them. Such action is not a transaction, but comes from reverence and obedience to God.

God reminded them that he had rescued them from Egypt and given them the land of Canaan as an inheritance. So those who have received grace should treat others with kindness. True faith shows not only in worship, but in living out selfless love and compassion in daily life.
a: Learn to help those in need without conditions
Don’t count gain and loss or profit, but look at every brother in difficulty with God’s love.
Act in the fear of God
Build your attitude and conduct on reverence for God, giving not reluctantly but gladly and willingly.
Live as one who has received grace
Remember that you are redeemed, and so support others with a compassionate heart, letting God’s grace flow out.
q: When I see someone near me in need, is my heart cold or compassionate?
Do I put my fear of God into practice by caring for and helping others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for redeeming me by grace and giving me an inheritance and hope. Teach me not to look coldly on those in need, but with reverence for You to gladly reach out a hand. Let me live as one who has received grace, and honor Your name in love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: A Reborn Life with a Living Hope
v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy became our father again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
Wherein you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been put to grief in various trials,
that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ;
whom not having seen you love; in whom, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy unspeakable and full of glory;
receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
b: Peter reminds us that our hope today is not an empty self-comfort, but is founded on the power of Jesus Christ’s resurrection from the dead. This is not philosophy or emotional expression; it is the rebirth of the spirit brought about by historical fact. We can have a “living hope” because our life has been changed: no longer the old self’s self-centeredness, but the new self’s selflessness, received anew in Christ.

This hope is not temporary; it is an imperishable inheritance kept in heaven. It is a glorious inheritance in God’s divine order, grace that the Heavenly Father has kept for us, beyond the decay and temptations of the world. When we face suffering and trials on earth, we do not hold on by ourselves; because the Holy Spirit is our guide, we are kept by God.

Trials may bring us grief, but they are the furnace that refines faith. Just as gold shows its purity through fire, faith shows its worth through testing. This process teaches us to let go of clinging to self, to deny ourselves and live, to let Jesus be King and to live a selfless life. Only through selflessness can Christ live in me, so that our focus is no longer on suffering but on the glorious Christ.

Though we have not seen him, we love him and look to him by faith, and this faith becomes the key to the salvation of our souls. This is exactly the practice of the three foundations: Jesus is my example, so I follow his obedience and suffering; the Bible is my standard, so I believe God’s promises will not fail; the Holy Spirit is my guide, so I rely on him firmly and do not waver.
a: See eternity and don’t be trapped by the temporary
Turn your focus from present suffering to the eternal inheritance, and trust the Lord who raises the dead.
Choose trust and obedience in trials
Believe in God’s keeping, and let trials forge a deeper faith rather than become a stumbling block.
Live selflessly and become a victor
When we lay down self and let Christ reign, we experience a transformation of the whole person: from mindset to life to daily living.
q: Am I currently living in a “self-centered” pattern of life? Do I still face difficulties in my own way?
In the trials of faith, have I let Jesus be King and let the Holy Spirit guide me, instead of relying on my own cleverness and will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving me new birth through Jesus Christ and a living hope. Help me not to shrink back in trials, but to be refined by You and have my faith strengthened. May my life no longer be me living, but Jesus living in me, so that I deny myself, live selflessly, and walk in Your will. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Learning to Praise in the Midst of Sorrow
v: Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived and bore a son, and she named him Reuben (meaning “a son”), for she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction; for now my husband will love me.”
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Because Yahweh has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon (meaning “hearing”).
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now this time will my husband be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore she named him Levi (meaning “joined”).
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “This time I will praise Yahweh.” Therefore she named him Judah (meaning “praise”). Then she stopped bearing.
b: Leah lived in a marriage where she was overlooked, carrying the pain of being ignored. But the Lord saw her suffering, had compassion on her, and enabled her to bear sons. With each child, Leah’s heart slowly changed: from hoping that her sons would win her husband’s love, to finally turning her focus to the Lord and praising him.

The birth of Judah marked a breakthrough in Leah’s faith. She no longer clung to the acceptance of people, but found her joy in God alone. No matter how people treat us, God’s eyes are always upon us. He listens, he understands, he gives grace, so that even in sorrow we can learn to praise.
a: Believe that God hears our sorrow
Even when people seem to overlook us, God still sees us and has compassion on us. He is a very present help at all times.
Turn from human expectations to God
Do not rest the worth of your life on people. Fix your eyes on God and seek his approval and love.
Learn to praise in hardship
Even when circumstances are difficult, learn to praise God, because praise frees our hearts from bitterness and turns them toward freedom and joy.
q: When I feel ignored or unloved, do I remember that God is still watching over me?
Am I willing to let my heart be released from human expectations and seek only God’s pleasure?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for hearing my cry even in my loneliest and most overlooked moments. Help me not to place my hope in people, but to look to You alone. Even in hard times, help me, like Leah, to learn to praise You and to rejoice in Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Beware the Trap of Greed
v: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, be merry.”’
But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
b: A man in the crowd called out, asking Jesus to bring justice by making his brother divide the family inheritance. But Jesus did not answer as he expected. Instead, he exposed a more dangerous problem deep in the human heart: greed. He told a parable about a rich man whose land produced abundantly. The man planned to build bigger barns and enjoy a comfortable life, never imagining that his soul would be taken that very night.

Jesus showed that a person’s life does not consist in how much he owns, but in whether he is rich in his relationship with God. The rich man wrongly fixed his focus on people, things, circumstances, and himself, and not on Jesus as the center of everything. Such a life looks abundant, but is in fact poor.

Jesus warned his disciples, “So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.” God does not care about the numbers in our accounts, but about the direction and motives of our hearts. When we let Jesus be King and place all our possessions and plans in his hands, we can escape the snare of greed and enter true abundance and freedom.
a: Discern where your heart is focused:
Are we chasing money, security, or career success so much that we neglect intimacy with God? If our focus is not on Jesus, our life will go astray.
Practice a selfless life:
Manage your time, money, and gifts as a trust rather than as something you own. That is selflessness, and it brings glory to God and blessing to others.
Let Jesus be King over your finances:
Are you willing to let the Lord govern your financial plans, including giving, self-restraint, and care for the poor? These are all part of God’s divine order.
q: When I face financial decisions or plan my life, do I put the Lord’s will first?
What in my life is like “pulling down my barns to build bigger ones”? Am I willing to let go and entrust it to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, guard my heart so that I am not blinded by possessions or lost in passing abundance. Help me to depend wholly on You and to honor You as great in every choice. May I be Your faithful steward, using what You have given me to glorify Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Helping Your Brother with Love
v: “‘If your brother becomes poor, and his hand fails with you, then you shall uphold him. He shall live with you as a stranger and a sojourner.
Take no interest from him, nor profit; but fear your God, that your brother may live with you.
You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.
I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.’”
b: God taught Israel that if a brother among them fell into hardship through poverty, they must not stand by and watch him perish, much less take advantage of him for profit. Instead, they were to help him in love, welcoming and supporting him as they would a sojourner. Such action does not come from a transaction, but from reverence and obedience toward God.

God reminded them that he had rescued them from Egypt and given them the land of Canaan as an inheritance. Therefore, those who have received grace should treat others with kindness. The reality of faith is shown not only in worship, but in living out selfless love and compassion in everyday life.
a: Learn to help those in need without conditions
Do not count gains and losses, but look at every brother in difficulty with God’s love.
Act out of reverence for God
Build your attitudes and actions on the fear of the Lord, giving not out of obligation but willingly and gladly.
Live as one who has received grace
Remember that you have been redeemed, and so support others with a compassionate heart, letting God’s grace flow through you.
q: When I see someone in need around me, is my heart cold or compassionate?
Do I put my reverence for God into practice by caring for and helping others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for redeeming me by Your grace and giving me an inheritance and hope. Teach me not to look coldly on those in need, but with a heart that fears You, to reach out gladly to help. Let me live as one who has received grace, and glorify Your name in love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Crying Out to God in Distress
v: Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the house of Yahweh, and spread it before Yahweh.
Hezekiah prayed before Yahweh, and said, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, who sit above the cherubim, you are the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, Yahweh, and hear. Open your eyes, Yahweh, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God.
Truly, Yahweh, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands,
and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone. Therefore they have destroyed them.
Now therefore, Yahweh our God, save us, I beg you, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Yahweh, are God alone.”
Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard you.’”
b: When Hezekiah faced the threat of Sennacherib, king of Assyria, he did not rely on his own strategy or military might. He immediately brought the crisis before the Lord. He spread the threatening letter out before God and cried out with a focused heart, acknowledging God as the ruler over all nations.

Hezekiah knew clearly that the enemy was insulting not merely his people, but the living God. He asked God to stretch out his hand and save, not only to be delivered from danger himself, but so that all the kingdoms of the earth would know that the Lord alone is God. God heard his prayer and gave a confirming reply through the prophet Isaiah.
a: Hand your burdens directly to God
When trouble comes, do not carry the anxiety yourself. Learn from Hezekiah to spread everything out before God and simply look to him.
Lift up God’s glory in prayer
Prayer is not only asking for our own needs to be met, but also for God’s name to be glorified, so that others come to know him through our testimony.
Trust that God will surely hear prayer
However difficult the situation, trust that God delights to hear the prayers of his children offered in faith, and that in his own time he will bring about the best deliverance.
q: When I face threats or difficulties, do I learn to go to God first?
Does my prayer focus only on my own needs, or is the glory of God my greatest desire?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for hearing me every time I call. Teach me, in times of distress, not to lean on myself first, but to spread my burdens out before You alone. May my life and my prayers always aim at Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Experiencing Perfect Power in Weakness
v: It is doubtless not profitable for me to boast, but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who was caught up into the third heaven fourteen years ago. Whether in the body, I don’t know, or whether out of the body, I don’t know; God knows.
I know such a man (whether in the body, or outside of the body, I don’t know; God knows)
how he was caught up into Paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in my weaknesses.
For if I would desire to boast, I will not be foolish; for I will speak the truth. But I refrain, so that no man may think more of me than that which he sees in me, or hears from me.

Because of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively.
Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather boast in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.
b: Paul shared the great revelations he had received in Christ, even being caught up to the third heaven. At the same time, he admitted that a “thorn” had been given to him in the flesh, to keep him from becoming proud of his spiritual experiences. That thorn became his weakness, his pain, and the focus of his prayer.

Paul asked the Lord three times to take the thorn away, but the Lord’s answer was, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” So Paul stopped complaining about his weakness and instead boasted in it with joy, because he knew that it is exactly when we are helpless that the power of Christ is fully displayed.
a: Accept your imperfection
Each of us has weaknesses and limits. We do not need to hide them or feel inferior, because this is the very space in which God works.
Look to Christ’s power in weakness
We do not rely on our own strength, but trust in the grace of Christ and experience his great power and support in difficulty.
Turn hardship into a joyful testimony
Every distress, persecution, and pain is a chance for God to show his faithfulness and power, teaching us to rejoice even in trials.
q: Am I still troubled or ashamed by some “thorn” and unwilling to place it in God’s hands?
When I face difficulty, do I complain, run away, or learn to rely on God and experience his grace and power?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that Your grace is sufficient for me. Even with my weakness and struggles, You show Your perfect power. Help me not to run away or boast in myself, but to rely on You humbly at all times and turn every challenge into a chance to testify to Your great power. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Preparing the Way of the Lord for Greater Grace
v: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets, “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you:
the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’”
John came, who baptized in the wilderness and preached the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
John was clothed with camel’s hair and wore a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
b: The Gospel of Mark opens by declaring that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, who brings the Good News of salvation. John the Baptist fulfilled the prophecy as the voice crying in the wilderness, preparing the way of the Lord. He called people to repent, to confess their sins, and to be baptized in water, preparing them for the greater salvation to come.

John saw himself as lowly and stressed that he was only the forerunner. The one who was truly coming was “mightier,” Jesus Christ. He does not only baptize, but renews hearts by the Holy Spirit, bringing true forgiveness and new birth.
a: Prepare your heart to welcome the Lord
Each day, clear away the obstacles in your heart with repentance, so that you become good soil for God’s work.
Admit your limits and inadequacy
Like John the Baptist, humbly acknowledge that we are only servants of God’s grace, and keep our focus on glorifying Christ rather than ourselves.
Long to be renewed by the Holy Spirit
Do not stop at outward change, but long for the inner renewal and filling of the Holy Spirit, so that your life truly shows the likeness of Christ.
q: Do I prepare my heart each day to welcome the Lord Jesus’ work in my life?
Do I long to be filled more with the Holy Spirit and live a life of true victory?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus Christ to save us. Help me to prepare my heart continually and turn back to You in repentance, and may the Holy Spirit renew me every day so that my life glorifies Your name. Like John the Baptist, may I humble myself and honor the Lord as great. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Trust in the Lord Wholeheartedly, Not in Your Own Understanding
v: My son, don’t forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments,
for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear Yahweh, and depart from evil.
It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.
b: King Solomon speaks in the tone of a father to his son, urging us that a truly blessed and wise life is found not in leaning on our own understanding, but in trusting wholeheartedly in God’s instruction and guidance. He teaches us to keep God’s commandments in our hearts and bind them around our necks, which means letting God’s word become the standard we can see and use at any moment in daily life.

When we learn to “trust in the Lord with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding,” we choose an attitude of fearing God and honoring him as Lord. This is in fact a selfless choice: we no longer let self run everything, but “acknowledge him” in all things, believing that he will surely direct the road ahead. Such a life does not rely on a clever mind, but opens a soft heart to seek the Lord, who is full of love and wisdom.
a: Keep God’s word as the standard of life

Do not remember God’s word only at worship or while reading Scripture, but “bind it around your neck and write it on the tablet of your heart,” so that it becomes the starting point for every choice and reaction.
Give up your own wisdom and turn to God’s heart
When facing a decision, do not let “your own understanding” set the course. Quiet yourself and pray for God’s leading. This is the practical way to fear him and obey him.
Let God be King in everything
In family, relationships, service, or work, invite God in as Lord. When you acknowledge him in everything, you will see him make your path straight and secure, and you will be blessed.
q: Recently, in what matter have I still been leaning on my own understanding instead of seeking God’s will?
Am I willing to acknowledge him in matters great and small, and let him be Lord?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I no longer want to live by my own understanding. I want to trust in You with all my heart and acknowledge Your authority in everything. Lead me on the straight path, help me to treasure Your word in my heart, and teach me to fear You with a humble and obedient heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: From Chaos to Order: Let God’s Word Be the Beginning of Creation
v: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness.
God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.
God said, “Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.”
God made the expanse, and divided the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse; and it was so.
God called the expanse “sky”. There was evening and there was morning, a second day.
God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear;” and it was so.
God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the waters he called “seas”. God saw that it was good.
God said, “Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, with its seed in it, on the earth;” and it was so.
The earth yielded grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, with its seed in it, after their kind; and God saw that it was good.
There was evening and there was morning, a third day.
b: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. This is no fairy-tale opening, but the foundation of faith. When everything was still chaos, darkness, and emptiness, God’s Spirit moved and God’s word went out: “Let there be light,” and there was light. From darkness to light, from disorder to order, from emptiness to fullness, the whole work of creation is a display of God’s word and God’s sovereignty.

This passage does not merely record a starting point in the past; it shows us how our lives are renewed today. When our hearts are empty, confused, and lost, that is the moment for God’s Spirit to move and God’s word to speak. He does not step in by force, but sets change in motion by speaking. It is a gentle yet authoritative rule, and it echoes our call to a selfless choice today: laying down our own chaos and judgments, and letting God’s word be the source from which order is created in our lives.
a: Let God’s word be the starting point of a new day

As on the first day of creation God said, “Let there be light,” you can say at the start of a new day, “Lord, I want you to shine and set my direction for today.” Seek God’s word first, and order and light come first.
Believe that God can turn chaos into beauty

Perhaps your life feels like “the earth was formless and empty, darkness on the surface of the deep,” but God’s Spirit is quietly at work. Do not rely on your own cleverness to fix everything; wait in faith for God’s word to come, and let him bring new order and life.
Learn to live by the rhythm God designed

Every day of creation had an evening and a morning, and God made sky, land, sea, and plants, each “after their kind.” He did not rush; he arranged things step by step. This reminds us to follow God’s pace and not chase the world’s tempo.
q: Am I willing, in chaos or in low places, to wait for God’s word to re-create my life?
In what area do I always want to arrange things myself, forgetting to let God speak and rule first?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for creating heaven and earth by Your word. May You speak in my heart today, driving away darkness and establishing order. Help me lay down my own confusion and impatience, and choose to be selfless and obedient to the rhythm of Your word. May I start each day with You and live out the beauty You have created. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Walking Together in Unity: A Stronger Bond
v: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
Again, if two lie down together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
If one prevails against him, two will withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
b: This passage shows the strength of walking together: someone to lift us when we fall, warmth for one another in the cold, and mutual support in the battle. From the beginning, God did not create people to walk alone, but invited them into relationships of unity. This applies not only to marriage but also to mutual help in spiritual community. When we are willing to lay down the pride of walking alone and choose humble connection, this is a selfless choice: admitting that we need others, and need the connections God has established.

In God’s divine order, supporting one another is an essential grace and wisdom. If we focus only on ourselves and refuse unity, life becomes lonelier and the fight harder. But when we learn to fear God and trust wholeheartedly in his design, no longer relying on our own judgment and strength but joining with the body to walk together, we will experience the real power of “a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”
a: Find companions for the journey

Do not fight alone. The church, fellow believers, and spiritual companions the Lord has given us are there so that we can hold each other up and build each other up on the road of faith. Find someone you can open up to, pray with, and walk the path of faith with.
Support one another in falling, without judging
When others are weak, do not rush to blame; be the one who “lifts up his fellow.” This is selflessness and compassion in practice, and a loving expression that pleases the Lord.
Learn to fight together in unity, not on your own

In family, service, or work, do not go it alone. Invite God to be your “third strand,” and invite faithful companions to join with you, and you will find that heavenly power is far greater than what you can do alone.
q: In what areas am I used to facing things alone, without learning to connect and walk with others?
When I fall or grow weary, who can I turn to for help? Am I also willing to be help to others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing me that You did not create me to walk alone, but to live in connection and mutual support. Help me to learn humility, not to rely on myself, and to be willing to walk with others, to be lifted up when I fall, and not to be alone in the battle. May I also be a help in the lives of others, living out the unity and blessing You designed. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Do Not Fear, for I Am with You
v: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be as nothing, and will perish.
You will seek them, and won’t find them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as nothing, as a non-existent thing.
For I, Yahweh your God, will hold your right hand, saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid. I will help you.’
b: When fear and pressure rush over us like ocean waves, God gives us more than a word of comfort. He personally promises, “I am with you” and “I will help you.” This is not a guarantee that we will never suffer, but an assurance that we will not be swallowed up in suffering. God’s right hand is not only a symbol of power, but of righteous protection and support.

For those who trust in him, “do not fear” is not empty self-talk, but comes from the certainty of God’s presence. When we are willing to let go of our own methods and choose selflessness to rely on God, we turn to the Ruler who created heaven and earth and governs history, and let him guide us and hold our right hand through the storm and into safety.
a: When fear comes, do not rely on yourself; return first to God’s presence
Fear makes us instinctively want to take control, but God wants us to stop first and remember that he is with us. Learn to pray quietly first, rather than rushing to respond.
Let God’s promises become the strength for your actions
When God says, “I will help you,” it is not an empty word, but a ground for action when we face challenges. It is not because we can, but because he will.
Practice the selflessness of faith: hand over control and choose to trust
Trust is not escaping responsibility, but handing authority back from ourselves to God. When we do, we will find that God’s right hand has never left us.
q: What fear am I facing lately? Am I focusing on the circumstances rather than on God?
Am I willing, in fear, to learn selflessness and entrustment, and let God’s word be a lamp to my feet?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for telling me, “Do not fear, I am with you.” When I feel weak and dismayed, help me choose to rely on You, not on my own strength, but to take hold of Your right hand and go forward. May I learn the selflessness of faith, hand the control to You, and experience Your strengthening and help. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
